# SQL fact counters: one per line, label TAB pattern (Java regex). srcmorph counts the pattern's
# matches over the whole source file and writes them as exact facts before the AI summary.
# The [ignore] line runs first and reads the file as a lexer does, leftmost region first: it blanks
# -- comments, '...' string literals ('' and a backslash escape a quote, as in MySQL) and /* ... */
# block comments, keeping the line breaks, so a /* inside a string or a -- comment opens nothing. It
# keeps MySQL's /*! ... */ version comments and Oracle's /*+ ... */ hints, which hold real SQL. A /*
# or a ' literal that is never closed comments out the rest of the file, as PostgreSQL and MySQL read
# it (so a file of escaped quotes stays linear); a nested PostgreSQL comment ends at its first */, and
# PostgreSQL's 'C:\' reads as a literal that the backslash keeps open (as in MySQL). So that an apostrophe in another dialect's quoting opens no
# literal, it also blanks PostgreSQL's dollar quoting on one line ($$it's$$, $fn$...$fn$; a function
# body over several lines stays, its statements count), Oracle's q'[...]', q'{...}', q'!...!' and
# the like (N too), a "..." that holds an apostrophe (a MySQL string; a quoted identifier, which has
# none, stays, so INSERT "t" still counts) and MySQL's # comments (at a line start or after a blank
# or ;, not a T-SQL #temp table, nor PostgreSQL's #> and #- operators). Statements are counted where
# they start a line (after spaces or tabs, never across a line break, which keeps a long blanked
# region linear),
# case-insensitive, for PostgreSQL, MySQL, T-SQL and Oracle. An INSERT counts with or without INTO
# (MySQL, T-SQL), after an Oracle /*+ hint */ and as INSERT ALL / FIRST, not as the INSERT branch of
# a MERGE or a trigger's event list; SQLite's INSERT OR REPLACE and a view inside a mysqldump /*!50001
# */ comment are not seen. A TYPE BODY, a MATERIALIZED VIEW LOG, a DATABASE LINK and a DATABASE
# SCOPED CREDENTIAL are not counted; MariaDB's CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE, PostgreSQL's CREATE FOREIGN
# TABLE and T-SQL's COLUMNSTORE indexes are. "VALUES rows (approx)" counts the row tuples of VALUES
# lists (a tuple after VALUES or after "),"), so a multi-row INSERT counts every row, but not the
# VALUES(col) function of MySQL's ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE (after an =); rows an INSERT ... SELECT
# reads from a table are not seen, and a tuple nested inside a row counts once more.
# SqlFactPatternsTest pins every case.
[ignore] comments and string literals
INSERT statements
VALUES rows (approx)
tables
views
indexes
functions/procedures
triggers
types
ALTER TABLE
sequences
extensions
schemas and databases
packages and package bodies
